title: Rabia al-Adawiyya
summary: Rabia of Basra is remembered as an early woman Sufi who turned Sufi thought toward a mysticism centred on divine love. Later narratives, above all that of the poet Attar, describe her as an enslaved orphan who was freed by her master. Much of what is told of her is hagiography, so details remain uncertain.

uncertainty.note: Dated "between c. 717 and 801" by the University of Surrey blog; the life is known mainly through later hagiography.

where.modern_name: Basra, Iraq; pinned to her native city
where.historical_name: Basra, in the Abbasid-era Islamic caliphate (the sources say only that she was a native of Basra)

importance.justification: Early and widely remembered woman Sufi, credited with centring Sufi thought on love of God.

sources.title: Rabi'a al-Basri (Rabia al-Adawiyya)
sources.publisher: University of Surrey, Medieval Women blog

reviewer_note: Least certain of the set: the Surrey page quotes a scholar that everything known of her "has been constructed", and Attar (c. 1140s-1221) is the first to write her life. Dates come from one source; EBSCO gives no dates.
